display_name: Tyrrell's Vat 1 Semillon, New South Wales
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Tyrrell's Vat 1 Semillon ferments in old oak vats from the 1860s, a choice that preserves Hunter Valley's sandy loam purity without oak dominance. This 2016 vintage earned a gold medal at TEXSOM, highlighting its lanolin texture and emerging honey notes. Age it further, and fig depth intensifies from the region's friable soils.",
  "wine_summary": "Tyrrell's crafts Vat 1 from century-old Semillon vines in Hunter Valley, where the producer pioneered single-vineyard labeling in Australia. This wine matters because it ages for decades, turning lean citrus into waxy richness that defines the region's whites. Hunter Valley's GI spans the Hunter River catchment, bounded by the Great Dividing Range, fostering Semillon with broad texture from its moderate acidity.",
  "terroir_expression": "Sandy alluvial loam and friable red duplex soils in Hunter Valley allow deep vine roots, yielding Semillon with lemon and lanolin up front that evolve into fig and beeswax. The subtropical climate with summer rains stresses vines, concentrating flavors into a waxy body, while deep friable loam retains enough moisture for low-vigor growth. Black silty loam over alkaline clay adds mineral grip, linking geology directly to the wine's textured palate.",
  "vinification_summary": "Tyrrell's picks grapes early for high acidity, crushes whole clusters, and ferments in neutral 150-year-old oak vats to avoid flavor imprint while allowing slow malolactic conversion in some years. No lees stirring emphasizes terroir clarity. This barrel-ferment technique, using vessels large enough for minimal wood contact, builds the wine's oxidative edge and longevity.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken cuts through the wine's waxiness with spice, while lemon notes echo the bird's brine. Grilled sardines with lemon and herbs match the Semillon's acidity and coastal minerality from Hunter soils. Fine dining: foie gras terrine pairs with emerging honey and lanolin, balancing fat against structure. Roast pork belly with apple slaw contrasts richness with the wine's fig depth. Oysters Kilpatrick amplify smoky salinity against broad texture.",
  "comparable_wines": "Chateau Climens 2010 — Sauternes Semillon benchmark with honeyed depth, but Vat 1 stays dry while matching aging poise. Yalumba Steeple Vineyard Semillon — Barossa counterpart with similar loam-driven wax, though less ageworthy.",
  "style_profile": "Semillon with medium body, moderate acidity, and waxy texture",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2016 from now through 2040; store cool at 55°F away from light. Earlier vintages like 2007 hit peak now.",
  "value_assessment": "$50-60 range positions Vat 1 against Hunter peers like Brokenwood ILR Semillon at $55. It outperforms on aging structure from old vines. Buy multiples for cellaring—medals confirm quality at this price.",
  "market_position": "Collectors chase back vintages on auction sites for their 20-year track record. Top Australian lists in New York and Sydney feature it for Semillon flights. Retail-savvy drinkers grab current releases under $60.",
  "insider_take": "Skip Vat 1 young unless you crave lime austerity—its genius unfolds after 10 years when lanolin dominates. Most chase flashier whites, missing this soil-driven transformer. Stock it if you value texture over fruit.",
  "aging_potential_years": 30,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 8,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 40,
  "sensory": {

}
